title: I ran one set of opening range rules on NQ, ES and gold for six years. One made 139%, one lost money, and the fee bill came out three different sizes
author: person-person12
selftext:
I had only ever run this thing on NQ, so I had no idea whether I was looking at a strategy or just looking at NQ. So I changed nothing except the symbol.

Rules: 5 minute candles, the first 30 minutes of the session builds a range, the first close outside it takes the break, both directions, stop and target off the range, flat by the close, one contract from $100,000. January 2020 to August 2026. Commission and slippage charged on every fill, and all three ran in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) so the candles and the cost table were identical across them.

**NQ:** 1,667 trades, 53.75% wins, profit factor 1.10, finished at **$239,455**

**ES:** 1,692 trades, 51.06% wins, profit factor 0.99, finished at **$94,177**

**GC (gold):** 1,646 trades, 49.27% wins, profit factor 1.08, finished at **$154,950**

The trade counts land within 3% of each other, so this isnt one instrument barely triggering while another fires constantly. Its the same setup, the same number of times, for the same six years.

**\_\_\_\_**

The execution bill is the part I keep going back to. **$16,670 on NQ, $29,610 on ES, $41,150 on gold.**

On ES those trades made **23.79% before costs** and the account still finished **down 5.82%**, so the entire result of that run is the fee line. Gold made 96.1% gross and kept 54.95% of it. NQ paid the smallest bill of the three and its the only one that looks like a strategy on a chart.

ES and NQ track the same index family and one of them carries this idea while the other one hands it back in costs. Nothing about that is a property of the pattern.

**\_\_\_\_**

The drawdowns pull in the other direction. Gold's worst stretch was **21.90%**, against **52.51% on NQ** and **50.28% on ES**, on identical rules over identical candles. The version that made the most money is also the one that would have taken half the account off you on the way there, and gold, the weakest profit factor of the three, had the calmest curve by a wide margin.

Worth saying that all three are one contract on a hundred grand with no position sizing, no session filter and no trade limit, so none of these is something I would run. The point was to hold the rules still and move the instrument.
